newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark sets date for controversial Rushdie visit.
newsitem.headline: Denmark sets date for controversial Rushdie visit.

text.p: British author Salman Rushdie is to receive a literary award in Copenhagen next week despite a row over security precautions which almost brought down the Danish government.

A joint statement by the Danish Rushdie Committee, the Culture Ministry and Cultural Capital 96 said that the venue of the award ceremony would not be made public and Rushdie would be unavailable for interviews during his visit.
Rushdie is one of three winners of European Union prizes to be presented in Copenhagen, this year's European Cultural Capital.

"The EU's Aristeion Prize, The European Literature Prize and The European Translation Prize will be distributed at a ceremony in Copenhagen, Wednesday November 13...All three prizewinners ...will be present," the statement said.
It said that the location would be kept secret until the last moment and attendance would be by invitation only.

Indian-born Rushdie has lived in hiding and under guard since 1989 when Iranian revolutionary leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a fatwa or death sentence against him for his novel "The Satanic Verses", saying it blasphemed against Islam.

Last week Denmark told him not to come and collect his prize because it was unable to guarantee his safety, sparking a furious row in which the minority government was threatened with a vote of no confidence.

The threat was lifted on Thursday when the leader of a left-wing party holding pivotal seats in parliament said he was now satisfied the government had acted out of incompetence in seeking to put off Rushdie's trip, rather than according to a secret political agenda.
